sample: 302 posts, a deterministic 1-in-23 slice of the 6,982 Caraballeda posts, 2026-06-24 to 2026-07-01

themes.name: Personas afectadas
themes.definition: Structural node: what happened to the people the earthquake reached.
themes.applies_when: Never classify against this node directly — it groups the themes below it. Use the finest child that fits.

themes.name: Edificaciones e infraestructura
themes.definition: Structural node: what happened to buildings, roads and services.
themes.applies_when: Never classify against this node directly — it groups the themes below it. Use the finest child that fits.

themes.name: Solicitudes y llamados
themes.definition: Structural node: what people asked for.
themes.applies_when: Never classify against this node directly — it groups the themes below it. Use the finest child that fits.

themes.name: Respuesta institucional y operativa
themes.definition: Structural node: what responders, officials and outside help did.
themes.applies_when: Never classify against this node directly — it groups the themes below it. Use the finest child that fits.

themes.name: Rescate de animal
themes.definition: A specific animal was found or rescued alive from rubble.
themes.applies_when: The post asserts that a specific animal was found alive or rescued from a collapsed or damaged structure.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T4 (Persona rescatada con vida): T23 is scoped to animals, not people.

themes.name: Persona rescatada con vida
themes.definition: A specific person was pulled out from rubble or a collapse site alive.
themes.applies_when: The post asserts that a named or described person was extracted/rescued alive from a collapsed or damaged structure.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T3 (Persona atrapada con vida): T4 requires the extraction itself to be asserted, not just that the person is alive and still trapped.

themes.name: Persona atrapada con vida bajo escombros
themes.definition: A specific person is currently alive and trapped under rubble.
themes.applies_when: The post asserts that a named or described person remains alive under rubble right now — e.g., voice or phone contact was established, sounds/movement were detected, or the post explicitly says they are trapped but alive.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T4 (Persona rescatada con vida): T3 is the standing condition of still being trapped; T4 requires the extraction itself to be asserted. T6 (Búsqueda sin señales de vida) is the opposite finding.

themes.name: Persona desaparecida o sin contacto
themes.definition: A specific named or described person has not been reached or located since the earthquake, and their fate is unknown.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a specific person's whereabouts are unknown or that contact with them has been lost since the earthquake (a missing-person report or a family statement that they cannot reach someone).
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T12 (Solicitud de información): T2 requires the post to assert that contact/whereabouts are actually lost; T12 covers a post that only asks whether anyone has news, without itself asserting the person is unreachable.

themes.name: Solicitud de información
themes.definition: A request asking whether anyone has news about a specific person, building, or place, without itself asserting what happened to them.
themes.applies_when: The post asks if anyone has information about a named person, building, or place, and does NOT itself assert that the person is missing, trapped, hurt, or dead — only that the asker currently lacks news.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T2 (Persona desaparecida): if the post also states contact has been lost, tag T2 as well; T12 alone applies to a bare inquiry.

themes.name: Colapso estructural
themes.definition: A specific building or piece of infrastructure came down (fully or partially collapsed).
themes.applies_when: The post states that a specific named building, residence, hotel, or piece of infrastructure (e.g., a bridge) collapsed, fell, or came down.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T10 (Daño sin colapso): T9 requires the structure to have actually come down, not merely been affected or damaged.

themes.name: Sismo o réplica registrada
themes.definition: A specific earthquake or aftershock event is reported (its occurrence, time, or magnitude).
themes.applies_when: The post states that a specific earthquake or aftershock occurred, citing its time, magnitude, or epicenter.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T9 (Colapso estructural): tag both if the post also asserts the quake/aftershock caused a specific collapse.

evidence.named_b: Terremoto: relato o resumen del evento

themes.name: Apoyo internacional desplegado
themes.definition: A specific country's or organization's rescue/aid team is present in, or was sent to, the disaster zone.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a named foreign country, government, or organization sent, deployed, or has personnel/equipment present in the affected area.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T16 (Operación en curso): T17 is about which country/organization is involved; T16 is about the activity/status at a site. Both may apply to one post.

evidence.named_b: Operación de búsqueda y rescate en curso

themes.name: Crítica o denuncia de la respuesta
themes.definition: An opinion, complaint, or accusation about who is (or is not) helping, or about how the response is handled.
themes.applies_when: The post expresses a critical, accusatory, or evaluative opinion about the disaster response — inaction, obstruction, corruption, or a comparison to how it should be handled — without itself being a request or a new factual claim about a person or building.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T20 (Declaración oficial): T19 is the author's own critical viewpoint; T20 reports what an official said or announced.

evidence.named_b: Crítica u opinión sobre la respuesta institucional
evidence.named_c: Denuncia de obstrucción o inacción de autoridades

themes.name: Mensaje de solidaridad, fe o aliento
themes.definition: A post expressing emotional support, prayer, gratitude, or encouragement about the disaster, without asserting a specific new fact.
themes.applies_when: The post's content is substantially a prayer, message of hope, gratitude, solidarity, or encouragement directed at the disaster, its responders, or its victims in general, and does not otherwise assert a specific fact captured by another theme.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Residue ('none'): a bare link, photo, or place tag with no expressed sentiment and no assertion is residue, not T27 — T27 requires actual expressed sentiment in the text.

evidence.named_b: Expresión de fe, esperanza o solidaridad
evidence.named_c: Expresión de duelo, fe o solidaridad

themes.name: Lista o directorio compilado
themes.definition: The post's main content is a compiled list of multiple people, buildings, or a shelter roster, rather than a report about one specific case.
themes.applies_when: The post's primary content is a compiled list of three or more named people, buildings, or locations (a roster of collapsed buildings, a shelter's occupant list, a list of missing persons).
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T9 or T2: a list can also carry T9/T2 if it substantively asserts those facts about its items, but T24 marks it as a compiled reference.

themes.name: Declaración o cifra oficial
themes.definition: An official or authority is reported as having made a statement or announced figures about the disaster.
themes.applies_when: The post reports that a named official, government body, or institution stated something, or announced a casualty/damage figure (deaths, injured, missing, homeless, economic loss).
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T19 (Crítica): T20 is reporting the official's own statement/figures, not the poster's opinion.

evidence.named_b: Balance oficial de víctimas y daños

themes.name: Entrega de ayuda humanitaria
themes.definition: Aid, supplies, or services were actually delivered or set up at a location.
themes.applies_when: The post states that supplies, equipment, medical care, electricity, connectivity, or another concrete service was delivered, installed, or made available at a specific location — not merely requested.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T13 (Solicitud de rescate o recursos): T18 requires delivery to be asserted as having happened; T13 is the request for it.

evidence.named_c: Solicitud o punto de insumos humanitarios

themes.name: Búsqueda sin señales de vida
themes.definition: Search teams found no signs of life at a specific site, or the search there was suspended or moved elsewhere.
themes.applies_when: The post states that rescuers found no indication of survivors at a specific site, or that the search/rescue effort there was called off, paused, or redirected to another building.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: T5 (Persona fallecida): T6 is a negative search result, not a confirmed death or body recovery. T3: opposite finding — signs of life.

evidence.named_b: Búsqueda concluida sin señales de vida
evidence.named_c: Labores de búsqueda y rescate en curso

themes.name: Persona fallecida
themes.definition: A specific person is reported or declared dead, whether or not a body has been found.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a named or described person died, was killed, or has been declared dead.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Cuerpo recuperado o identificado — that requires the body itself to have been found, recovered or identified. A person may be declared dead with no body.

evidence.why: A death and a body are not the same fact. As this ages, many will be declared dead with no body ever found or identified — a merged theme would silently conflate the two and the record could not tell them apart.

themes.name: Cuerpo recuperado o identificado
themes.definition: A body was physically recovered from a site, handed over, or identified.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a body was pulled from the rubble, recovered, handed over to relatives, or identified at a specific site.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Persona fallecida — a death may be reported or declared with no body found.

evidence.why: A death and a body are not the same fact. As this ages, many will be declared dead with no body ever found or identified — a merged theme would silently conflate the two and the record could not tell them apart.

themes.name: Solicitud de rescate
themes.definition: A call for rescuers to come to a site where someone is believed to be alive.
themes.applies_when: The post asks or urges that rescuers, teams or personnel be sent to a specific site because someone is, or may be, alive there.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Solicitud de recursos — that asks for things (machinery, fuel, tools, supplies), not for people to come and dig.

evidence.why: Asking for rescuers because someone may be alive is not asking for fuel. One is a life; the other is logistics.

themes.name: Solicitud de recursos
themes.definition: A call for machinery, fuel, tools, medical supplies or other material to be sent.
themes.applies_when: The post asks or urges that machinery, fuel, tools, medical supplies, water, food or other material be sent to a specific site or cause.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Solicitud de rescate — that asks for the rescuers themselves.

evidence.why: Asking for rescuers because someone may be alive is not asking for fuel. One is a life; the other is logistics.

themes.name: Operación de rescate con vida
themes.definition: Teams are working a site to reach someone believed or shown to be alive.
themes.applies_when: The post describes teams working a site to reach a person believed or shown to be alive — digging toward contact, a voice, or a located survivor.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Operación de recuperación de cuerpos — that is work where no survivor is expected.

evidence.why: Working to reach someone believed alive is not working to recover the dead. The operation, its urgency and its meaning for the record all differ.

themes.name: Operación de recuperación de cuerpos
themes.definition: Teams are working a site to recover the dead.
themes.applies_when: The post describes teams working a site to recover bodies, or working where the post says no survivor is expected.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Operación de rescate con vida — that is work toward someone believed alive.

evidence.why: Working to reach someone believed alive is not working to recover the dead. The operation, its urgency and its meaning for the record all differ.

themes.name: Apoyo desplegado
themes.definition: Structural node: who came to help, and from where.
themes.applies_when: Never classify against this node directly — it groups the themes below it. Use the finest child that fits.

evidence.why: International teams are the loudest but not the only ones. Locals trying to help, and national bodies deployed, are what was actually on the ground.

themes.name: Apoyo nacional desplegado
themes.definition: A Venezuelan national or regional body sent people or equipment to the area.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a Venezuelan body — a ministry, the armed forces, Bomberos, a state or municipal government — sent, deployed, or has personnel or equipment present in the affected area.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Apoyo internacional desplegado — that is a foreign country or organization.

evidence.why: International teams are the loudest but not the only ones. Locals trying to help, and national bodies deployed, are what was actually on the ground.

themes.name: Apoyo vecinal o voluntario
themes.definition: Neighbours, residents or self-organized volunteers are doing the work themselves.
themes.applies_when: The post states that neighbours, residents, volunteers or self-organized citizens are working at a site — clearing rubble by hand, digging, carrying, searching — rather than a deployed institution.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Apoyo nacional desplegado — that is an institution with a name and a chain of command.

evidence.why: International teams are the loudest but not the only ones. Locals trying to help, and national bodies deployed, are what was actually on the ground.

themes.name: Ayuda humanitaria
themes.definition: Structural node: the aid chain — gathered, moved, delivered.
themes.applies_when: Never classify against this node directly — it groups the themes below it. Use the finest child that fits.

evidence.why: Aid is a chain, not an event: gathered, moved, delivered. Citizens self-organize collection points and the distribution effort is its own work.

themes.name: Centro de acopio
themes.definition: A collection point for donated goods exists, was set up, or changed what it accepts.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a collection point (centro de acopio) exists, was opened or closed, is receiving goods, or has stopped receiving them, at a named location.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Entrega de ayuda humanitaria — that is aid reaching the people it is for.

evidence.why: Aid is a chain, not an event: gathered, moved, delivered. Citizens self-organize collection points and the distribution effort is its own work.

themes.name: Logística y distribución de ayuda
themes.definition: Gathered aid was moved, routed or handed between organizations.
themes.applies_when: The post states that aid already gathered was transported, flown, shipped, convoyed, routed or handed from one organization to another — the movement itself, not the gathering or the final delivery.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Centro de acopio (the gathering) and Entrega de ayuda humanitaria (the final delivery).

evidence.why: Aid is a chain, not an event: gathered, moved, delivered. Citizens self-organize collection points and the distribution effort is its own work.

themes.name: Damnificados y refugio
themes.definition: People lost their homes, were displaced, or are staying in a shelter.
themes.applies_when: The post states that people lost their home, were displaced, evacuated, or are staying in a shelter, refuge or another household.

evidence.why: Cut by my two-of-three-readers threshold, which filters by SAMPLE SIZE, not by reality. The full corpus carries it (damnificados 40, refugio 24, and every reader had a damage-without-collapse theme that the post-overlap match failed to pair).

themes.name: Daño estructural sin colapso
themes.definition: A named structure was damaged or made unsafe but did not come down.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a named structure was damaged, cracked, tilted, or declared unsafe, and did NOT collapse.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Colapso estructural — that requires the structure to have actually come down.

evidence.why: Cut by my two-of-three-readers threshold, which filters by SAMPLE SIZE, not by reality. The full corpus carries it (damnificados 40, refugio 24, and every reader had a damage-without-collapse theme that the post-overlap match failed to pair).

themes.name: Seguridad y orden público
themes.definition: Structural node: what happened to safety and order in the aftermath.
themes.applies_when: Never classify against this node directly — it groups the themes below it. Use the finest child that fits.

evidence.why: A structural node so the two looting themes below it are not loose at the root. Mine, not the corpus's — discard it and reparent them if the shape is wrong.

themes.name: Saqueo de comercios
themes.definition: A shop, pharmacy, bakery or other business was looted after the earthquake.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a specific named business or commercial premises was looted, is being looted, or was emptied by a crowd.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Saqueo de viviendas — that is homes and vehicles, not businesses. And a post that only DENOUNCES looting in general, naming nothing, is «Crítica o denuncia de la respuesta».

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Saqueos en comercios afectados por el sismo en La Guaira, incluyendo Farmatodo en Caribe, Farmatodo de Los Corales, panadería Karol en Palmar Este, Farmatodo de Tanaguarena, y un negocio en la calle Real de Caraballeda.
evidence.why: Reached by the extractor's `unfitted` list on 20 looting posts, in 3 of 3 identical runs. Nobody wrote this theme from a desk — it is the corpus asking for a word it does not have.

themes.name: Saqueo de viviendas
themes.definition: Homes, apartments or vehicles in a damaged building were looted — often once the rescuers had gone.
themes.applies_when: The post states that apartments, homes or vehicles at a named building or street were looted or robbed after the earthquake.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Saqueo de comercios — that is businesses. The timing, when the post gives it, belongs in the claim's nuance rather than in the choice of theme.

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Saqueos en el edificio Golf Mar tras la búsqueda de rescatistas. / Robo y saqueo en apartamentos y carros del edificio Golf Mar tras la búsqueda.
evidence.why: Reached by the extractor's `unfitted` list on 20 looting posts, in 3 of 3 identical runs. Nobody wrote this theme from a desk — it is the corpus asking for a word it does not have.

themes.name: Estado de los servicios básicos
themes.definition: Water, power, telephone or internet service was lost, or is reported still working, somewhere named.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a basic service — water, electricity, telephone, internet, a telecom repeater — failed, was restored, or is the only one still working, at a named place.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Daño estructural sin colapso — that is the fabric of a building; this is the service reaching it.

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Una repetidora de telecomunicaciones en Caribe es la única que funciona para comunicación con familiares. / En Caraballeda no hay agua ni sitios donde comprar porque todo está saqueado.
evidence.why: Reached by the extractor's `unfitted` list on 20 looting posts, in 2 of 3 identical runs. Nobody wrote this theme from a desk — it is the corpus asking for a word it does not have.
evidence.also: Reader A proposed `Servicios básicos caídos` in the 2026-07-27 spike and my two-of-three-readers threshold cut it — the THIRD real theme that threshold lost, after `Damnificados y refugio` and `Daño estructural sin colapso`. The corpus has now asked for it directly.

themes.name: Colapso o cierre de vía o puente
themes.definition: A road, bridge or access route came down, was blocked, or was closed.
themes.applies_when: The post states that a named road, avenue, bridge or access route collapsed, was blocked by rubble or a landslide, or was closed to traffic.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Colapso estructural — that is a building. This is the way to it.

evidence.proposed_by: two of three spike readers, at overlap 1.00 over 8 posts
evidence.why: Readers B and C both proposed `Colapso o cierre de infraestructura vial` and their post sets matched EXACTLY. It never reached the vocabulary because my consensus script iterated reader A's themes and asked how well B and C matched each — so a theme A did not have was invisible however perfectly the other two agreed. A method bug, not a threshold one.

themes.name: Obra para restablecer el acceso
themes.definition: Work was done to reopen a route — a temporary bridge moved in, rubble cleared from a road, a way reopened.
themes.applies_when: The post states that work is under way or completed to restore access to a place: a provisional or military bridge moved, installed or opened; a road cleared; a route reopened.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Colapso o cierre de vía o puente — that is access LOST; this is access being given back. And `Logística y distribución de ayuda` is moving aid, not building the way for it.

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Se desmonta un puente de guerra en El Rosal para ser llevado a Caraballeda.
evidence.why: The FIRST batch read from a different day — 2026-06-29, day five — asked for this on its first run. Reader C also had a temporary-bridge post in its residue during the 2026-07-27 spike. Two mechanisms, two methods, two days, the same gap.

themes.name: Respuesta ausente o detenida
themes.definition: Rescuers or equipment have not reached a named place, or the work there has stalled for want of fuel, an operator or machinery.
themes.applies_when: The post states that at a named place no rescuers or machinery have arrived, or that work has stopped or cannot continue because fuel, an operator, equipment or personnel are missing. It REPORTS an absence; it does not ask for anything.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Solicitud de recursos and Solicitud de rescate — those ASK. This asserts that nothing has come, which is a fact about the world. Same line the whole vocabulary turns on.

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Una grúa de 100 toneladas está a 5 minutos del lugar donde se necesita, sin operador, desde hace más de 24 horas. / Se reporta que en Caraballeda hay rescatistas pero no combustible ni suficientes operadores de maquinaria. / en el edificio Rota Sol Place, avenida José María España Caraballeda, no han llegado rescatistas.
evidence.why: Six residue entries across three separate days (Jun 27, 28, 30), clustered rather than proposed one by one. The largest thing the vocabulary cannot hold.

themes.name: Obstrucción de la respuesta
themes.definition: Rescuers or aid were held, blocked, diverted or delayed by an authority or a third party.
themes.applies_when: The post states that rescuers, equipment or aid were detained, blocked, turned back, diverted or made to wait by an authority or anyone else — an event with a time and a place, not an opinion about the response.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Crítica o denuncia de la respuesta — that is the author's judgement of how things are going. This is something that was DONE to the response.

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Régimen retuvo 8 horas a rescatistas para un acto protocolar. / Un ciudadano ruso dio transporte a rescatistas retenidos.
evidence.why: Two residue entries, plus independent corroboration from the 2026-07-27 spike: reader B proposed `Obstrucción institucional` over 7 posts and marked it a HAPPENING, while reader C called the same thing a topic. That was the single nature disagreement in the entire spike — and the corpus has now settled it. Rescuers held for eight hours is an event.

themes.name: Colapso múltiple en una zona
themes.definition: Several buildings came down in a named area, without any one of them being identified.
themes.applies_when: The post states that more than one structure collapsed in a named sector, street, seafront or parish, without naming the individual buildings. A count ("tres edificios") is welcome but not required.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Colapso estructural — that needs a NAMED structure. This is the area-level report that rule refuses, and refusing it lost a real fact.

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Se reportan múltiples edificios colapsados en el malecón de Los Corales, La Guaira, sin especificar nombres. / Se reporta que tres edificios colapsaron en el sector Los Cocos de Caraballeda. / Se reportan múltiples edificios desplomados en Caraballeda, sin especificar nombres.
evidence.why: Five residue entries across two separate sweeps. This is the corpus pushing back on a rule I WROTE: I made «Colapso estructural» require a named structure, to stop a vivid word producing a phantom claim. The corpus reports collapse at the AREA level constantly — three buildings in Los Cocos, a whole seafront — and that is a real, countable, evidenced fact a memorial must hold. The rule was right and its scope was too narrow.

themes.name: Registro visual del daño
themes.definition: The post's content is a photograph or video of a place, and its text asserts nothing on its own.
themes.applies_when: The post publishes or points at an image or video of a named place — an aerial view, a street, a building — and the TEXT alone states no happening. Route it here; a text-only reading cannot see what the picture shows.
themes.not_to_be_confused_with: Colapso estructural and Colapso múltiple en una zona — if the TEXT itself states that something came down, that is a claim, whatever else the post carries.

evidence.proposed_by: the corpus, through the residue list
evidence.verbatim: Se publica una foto del edificio Albatros en Caraballeda. / Un video muestra múltiples edificios colapsados en el malecón de Los Corales, sin identificar nombres. / Se publica una vista aérea de La Guaira mostrando daños estructurales.
evidence.why: Eight residue entries across three sweeps, and rising as a share of it. This is the MODALITY gap the three-reader spike measured independently — six of its 302 posts were captions whose evidence sits in an image — and image reading is deliberately parked. A gap that is parked must still stop re-asking: a residue entry repeating every sweep is a queue, which is the one thing the report may not become. Naming it as a TOPIC routes those posts out of the residue, admits plainly that a text-only reading cannot see them, and makes them findable the day the images are read.

retired_by_operator_2026_07_28: Operación de búsqueda y rescate en curso
